Protocol Discovery

Robotics Fleet Floods Public Relays in Accidental P2P Signaling Proof

By Our Technology Correspondent · Dispatch
When Pollen Robotics released Microduck, an unannounced WebRTC signaling dependency routed thousands of ephemeral coordination events across open Nostr relays—triggering denial-of-service alarms that quickly turned into admiration.

What began yesterday morning as frantic chatter across Japanese relay dashboards—operators wondering whether open relay pools were suffering a distributed denial-of-service attack or being quietly exploited as an unmetered storage dump—ended with an unexpected demonstration of the protocol’s raw utility. A multiplayer robotics release titled Microduck, developed by Pollen Robotics, was discovered to be leaning on Trystero, a serverless WebRTC library that hardcodes public Nostr relays as its default peer-discovery and signaling layer.

Because the traffic consisted almost entirely of ephemeral matchmaking messages that are routed immediately and discarded without consuming disk space, the relays carried the entire burst without buckling. As the source of the traffic became clear, suspicion among developers transformed into quiet celebration: an external engineering project had selected Nostr not as an alternative social network, but purely as zero-configuration, censorship-resistant transport plumbing.

The incident underscored an argument long voiced across the developer community: the most consequential adoption of Nostr may happen far away from microblogging timelines. As reya observed during the debate, I've always believed that the 'other stuff' will make nostr win, not the 'twitter clone'.

Hardware Retrofit

Sixty-Year-Old Vending Machine Dispenses Cold Glass Bottles for Sats

Vancouver, B.C. · Reported by Leo · Field Report

In the downtown core of Vancouver, a mechanical relic from the 1960s has found a second life without altering its cooling system or classic coin-operated aesthetic. Members of the DCTRL hackerspace completed a retrofit on a vintage Coca-Cola vending machine, wiring a Raspberry Pi and a physical relay into the internal coin mechanism and connecting the trigger to LNbits.

Writing from the workshop floor, Leo reported on the finished build: This almost 60 year old vending machine only takes sats! After all that time, without a single Freon refill, it still dispenses ice cold Coca Cola glass bottles. It was surprisingly simple to retrofit, using a Raspberry Pi, a relay and LNbits.

Security Advisory

Core Lightning Issues Emergency Offline Flag

Librería de Satoshi · Advisory

Node operators across the Lightning Network received an urgent advisory to start existing Core Lightning daemons with the --offline command-line argument pending the release of signed update binaries. Releases 26.04 and earlier have reached end-of-life status, prompting educators to remind node maintainers that self-sovereignty requires timely maintenance.

Network Hygiene

The Recurring Vulnerability of Packet Sniffing

Warning by Matt Corallo · Notice

Following fresh reports of parser exploits, Bitcoin Core engineer Matt Corallo issued a blunt caution to system administrators inspecting network wire captures: This is your regular reminder not to use Wireshark to read untrusted packets.

Expanding on the hazard, Corallo noted that the software’s massive C codebase makes parser faults an ongoing reality: This is far from the first time wireshark has had a critical RCE vulnerability 😭. In fact far from it, they gave them every year or three.

Cybercrime

Australian Police Arrest Two Over npm Shai-Hulud Worm

Perth, Australia · Report

Australian federal authorities arrested two alleged members of the TeamPCP syndicate in Perth. The suspects, aged 21 and 23, have been tied to systematic supply chain compromises targeting JavaScript registries, including the automated propagation of the Shai-Hulud worm.

Alex71btc · Release v0.3.1

Version 0.3.1 of BOLT12 Pay landed on Umbrel and StartOS, adding a persistent contacts layer to transform raw nodes into everyday transactional wallets. The developer noted the driving goal was to make a self-hosted Lightning node feel more like a usable sovereign wallet, not just infrastructure.

Client Architecture

Nostur & Coracle Push Major Overhauls to Discovery and Comment Handling

Ecosystem Releases · Nostur · Coracle

Client development saw simultaneous major releases today. Nostur shipped v1.31.0, introducing a unified Web of Trust discovery toggle across media tabs, overhauled badge administration, and background video management.

Simultaneously, hodlbod published Coracle 0.6.36, which transitions kind 1 inline replies into dedicated thread comments, strips surveillance query tracking parameters from outbound web links, and resolves compose box line-wrapping bugs.
